note: GFx_DefineSubImageLoader (2012 0xa369d0), tag 1008. The six u16s were already read in the right order; what was missing is the one line the decompile ends with, `*((_DWORD *)v33 + 2) = v12 | 0x90000` - the second u16 is the atlas's INDEX and the base image is registered under `index | 0x90000`, the packed-image id space. Reading it bare asked the dictionary for a character id, and in UI_HUD atlas index 5 is character 5, an unrelated shape. All 184 sub-images of the movie failed

GFx_DefineExternalImageLoader2 (2012 0xa36210), tag 1009. Already ported; cited because it is the other half of the same id space. `sub_E2C3F0(v2, v6 & 0x9FFFF, ...)` - the u32 id masked with 0x9FFFF, and tag 1009's atlas entries carry flags 9 in the high half, so atlas index 5 is id 0x90005 and a `-nopack` image is its bare index
GSubImageInfo::GetWidth. Forwards to pBaseImage (this+12) through its vt[1], so for a sub-image it answers the SHEET's width, not the rectangle's. That is what makes the UV divisor the atlas size
GSubImageInfo::GetTexture. Forwards to pBaseImage's vt[3] - the sheet's texture, which is what a sub-image fill binds
GSubImageInfo::GetRect. Copies this+16..this+28, the rectangle inside the sheet. The origin the UV map adds

GImageInfoBase::GetRect - the base class arm, `(0, 0, GetWidth(), GetHeight())`. With GSubImageInfo's override this is one expression for both cases, uv = (GetRect().TopLeft + pixel) / GetWidth(), which is GFxImageCharacterDef::BuildPixelToUVMatrix

GFxDisplayContext::PushAndDrawMask (2012 0xa5f510). Increments GFxDisplayContext+148 for exactly as long as the mask character's own Display runs, between BeginSubmitMask (renderer vt+172, mode = MaskLevel != 0) and EndSubmitMask (vt+176). That counter is GFxDisplayContext::MaskDrawDepth here. NOTE: changing nothing measurable in this content - the HUD draws with or without it (agentEM.md 3.1)

GFxDisplayList::Display (2012 0x9d56c0). Its mask branch is `if (!ClipDepth || MaskDrawDepth) draw as content; else PushAndDrawMask` - a clip carrying a ClipDepth while a mask is being drawn is part of THAT mask's shape, not a nested one. This tree opened a nested mask there. NOTE: changing nothing measurable in this content

GFxSprite::Display (2012 0x9faeb0). Cited for what it does NOT contain: its only early-out is the visibility test `(flags & 3) != 1 && !(flags & 0x8000)` on this+160, and there is no alpha or Cxform test anywhere in its 690 bytes. The GFxDisplayCxformIsTransparent early-out is agent EA's; this package stops it reaching a mask, whose alpha decides nothing because colour writes are off and whose absence empties the stencil
